source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: PDF p.15 Line 15 - Social security benefit exclusion; Form ND-1 line 15; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 100,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 125,500.00. Taxable Social Security 25,500.00 is the federal amount given (gross 30,000.00). Federal taxable income = 125,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 107,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 107,750.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 107,750.00. Subtractions: line 15 Social Security benefit exclusion, the taxable amount on Form 1040 line 6b, 25,500.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 25,500.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 107,750.00 - 25,500.00 = 82,250.00. Line 19 = 82,250.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (82,250.00 - 48,475.00) = 1.95% x 33,775.00 = 658.6125, to the cent 658.61; the Tax Table row 82,250 to 82,300 gives 659; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: not a joint return, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 658.61.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
